t.pt: มาหา: dois verbos colados para 'vir ver alguém'
t.en: maa haa: two verbs glued together for 'come to see someone'

e.pt: O tailandês não usa preposição para dizer a quem a visita se dirige: มา ('vir') gruda direto em หา ('procurar, ir atrás') e a pessoa vem depois — มาหาใครคะ ('o senhor veio ver quem?'). É o mesmo molde do มาทำงาน da lição 15 e do ไปรับ da 9: verbo de movimento + verbo que diz o motivo, sem nenhum 'para' no meio. E a bússola continua sendo o falante: quem recebe diz มาหา, quem conta a própria ida diz ไปหา.
e.en: Thai needs no preposition for the person visited: มา 'come' is glued straight onto หา 'seek, look for', and the object follows — มาหาใครคะ 'who did you come to see?'. Same mold as มาทำงาน (lesson 15) and ไปรับ (lesson 9): motion verb + purpose verb, with no 'to' in between. The speaker's position still rules: the host says มาหา, the visitor talking about himself says ไปหา.

t.pt: ทราบ e รู้: o mesmo 'saber' em dois registros
t.en: ทราบ and รู้: one 'know' in two registers

e.pt: Os dois querem dizer saber um fato e em muita construção podem trocar de lugar; o que muda é o registro. ทราบ é a forma polida, de escritório e de balcão — por isso o visitante diz ทราบไหมครับ na recepção; entre amigos seria รู้ไหม. E há construções em que só o รู้ entra: รู้หนังสือ ('ser alfabetizado', na letra 'conhecer letra'), รู้ภาษาอังกฤษ ('saber inglês') e ไม่รู้เรื่อง ('não entender o que ele está dizendo'). Trocar ทราบ pelo รู้ nesses três casos não funciona.
e.en: Both mean 'to know a fact' and are often interchangeable; what changes is register. ทราบ is the polite, official form, which is why the visitor says ทราบไหมครับ at a reception desk, while among friends it would be รู้ไหม. Some constructions take only รู้: รู้หนังสือ 'to be literate', รู้ภาษาอังกฤษ 'to know English', ไม่รู้เรื่อง 'not to follow what someone is saying'.

notas.ex: คุณ|kun ทราบ|sâap ไหม|mǎi ครับ|kráp

t.pt: รู้จัก: conhecer gente e lugar, não saber fato
t.en: รู้จัก: to be acquainted with people and places

e.pt: Se ทราบ e รู้ dão conta de fatos, รู้จัก é o verbo da familiaridade: com gente, com lugar e com coisa. รู้จักคุณ ('conhecer você'), รู้จักสนามหลวง ('conhecer o Sanam Luang, saber onde fica'), รู้จักคำนี้ ('conhecer esta palavra'). É a nossa fronteira entre 'conhecer' e 'saber', e em tailandês ela é dura: รู้จัก não aceita uma frase inteira com ว่า dentro. Se o que você sabe é um fato, volte para รู้ ou ทราบ.
e.en: Where ทราบ and รู้ handle facts, รู้จัก handles familiarity — with a person, a place or a thing: รู้จักคุณ 'know you', รู้จักสนามหลวง 'know (where) Sanam Luang is', รู้จักคำนี้ 'be familiar with this word'. It maps the Portuguese conhecer versus saber split, and รู้จัก does not take a ว่า-clause: for a fact, go back to รู้ or ทราบ.

notas.ex: เขา|kǎo รู้จัก|rúu-jàk คุณ|kun

t.pt: Uma frase dentro da outra: o lugar entra depois do verbo
t.en: Sentence embedding: the place follows the verb

e.pt: O tailandês encaixa uma frase inteira dentro de outra sem conectivo nenhum. 'Ele está sentado' (เขานั่ง) somado a 'ele está lá na frente' (เขาอยู่ข้างหน้า) dá uma frase só: เขานั่งอยู่ข้างหน้า. O verbo de postura vem primeiro, e o อยู่ + lugar entra atrás dizendo onde a ação acontece — o mesmo vale para ยืน ('em pé'), นอน ('deitado') e para os outros verbos de movimento, como เข้าไป e มา. Pense em dois cartões sobrepostos: o de cima é a postura, o de baixo é o endereço.
e.en: Thai embeds a whole sentence inside another with no connector. 'He sits' (เขานั่ง) plus 'he is in front' (เขาอยู่ข้างหน้า) merge into เขานั่งอยู่ข้างหน้า: the posture verb comes first and อยู่ + place is embedded after it to locate the action. The same holds for ยืน, นอน and other motion verbs such as เข้าไป and มา.

notas.ex: เขา|kǎo นั่ง|nâng อยู่|yùu ข้างหน้า|kâang-nâa

t.pt: ว่า: o conectivo obrigatório da frase-objeto
t.en: ว่า: the obligatory connector of an object clause

e.pt: Verbos como ทราบ ('saber'), พูด ('falar'), คิด ('achar') e บอก ('avisar') não pedem um substantivo, pedem uma frase inteira — e o ว่า é o conectivo obrigatório quando o verbo vem antes: เขาบอกว่ากลับก่อนเที่ยง ('ele avisou que volta antes do meio-dia'), ผมทราบว่าเขาอยู่ที่ไหน ('sei onde ele mora'). Sem o ว่า a frase fica com duas metades soltas. Quando a pergunta vem antes do verbo, o ว่า pode cair: เขาอยู่ที่ไหน คุณทราบไหมครับ.
e.en: Verbs such as ทราบ 'know', พูด 'speak', คิด 'think' and บอก 'tell' take a whole sentence as object, and ว่า is the obligatory connector when the verb precedes it: เขาบอกว่ากลับก่อนเที่ยง 'he said he would be back before noon', ผมทราบว่าเขาอยู่ที่ไหน 'I know where he lives'. When the clause comes before the verb, ว่า may be dropped.

notas.ex: เขา|kǎo บอก|bɔ̀ɔk ว่า|wâa จะ|jà กลับ|glàp ก่อน|gɔ̀ɔn เที่ยง|tîiang

t.pt: ขอ: o pedido educado em três ordens
t.en: ขอ: the polite request in three word orders

e.pt: O ขอ ('pedir') transforma uma frase afirmativa em pedido, e o livro mostra as três ordens: ผมขอใช้โทรศัพท์, ขอผมใช้โทรศัพท์ e só ขอใช้โทรศัพท์ — as três valem 'posso usar o telefone?', sem diferença de sentido, e a terceira é a mais comum. O pronome só pode sumir quando é ผม ou ดิฉัน. O pedido costuma vir com หน่อยได้ไหมครับ no fim, e a resposta que concede é ได้ครับ ('pode'). É um 'por gentileza' que se encosta antes do verbo, não depois.
e.en: ขอ 'to request' turns a statement into a request, and the book gives all three orders: ผมขอใช้โทรศัพท์, ขอผมใช้โทรศัพท์ and just ขอใช้โทรศัพท์, all meaning 'may I use the telephone', with no difference in meaning — the third is probably the most common. The subject pronoun may be dropped only when it is ผม or ดิฉัน. The form often takes หน่อยได้ไหมครับ at the end, and the granting answer is ได้ครับ 'go ahead'.
